summary: Large invoice due to late usage postbacks from offline edge devices — request for adjustment and explanation
description:
Issue summary:
Customer SignalGrid reports a $12,300 unexpected charge on the monthly invoice dated 2026-02-28. The customer says most of their devices were offline for maintenance between 2026-02-20 and 2026-02-22; when devices came back online they uploaded queued inference results which appear to have been metered as new realtime requests instead of being deduplicated or attributed to the original batch window.

Impact:
- Immediate billing dispute: excess charge of ~$12.3k.
- Customer concerned about double-counting and incorrect attribution across regions.

Environment:
- Dedicated account on prod in us-west with burst routing to eu-west.
- Company uses SDK v1.8 with offline buffer and postback endpoint /v1/usage/postback.

Steps to reproduce (reported by customer):
1) Simulate device offline for 48 hours (devices buffer inference results locally).
2) Bring device online; SDK posts queued events to /v1/usage/postback in rapid succession.
3) Observe that metering records each postback as new realtime requests with full token counts (no dedupe).

Customer-provided logs & attachments:
- s3://sg-support-uploads/signalgrid/2026-02/postbacks/manifest.csv
- Screenshot of invoice line items (attached in ticket)
- Example postback HTTP payloads (postback_examples.txt)
comments: 2026-03-01 Priya Menon (Support): Received initial claim and escalated to Billing. Asked for billing window, sample postbacks and invoice PDF. Requested org-id and API-key hash for verification.

2026-03-01 Customer (SignalGrid - Tara Long): Provided invoice PDF and S3 manifest. Notes that the events show 'queued=true' in the SDK payload but billing still charged full real-time token price. Asked for provisional credit while investigating.

2026-03-02 Ethan Zhao (Billing Eng): Reproduced scenario in staging with SDK v1.8. Found that ingestion-service was marking postbacks without backlog header as realtime. Opened investigation with metersrv and ingestion teams. Tagged as Sev1 due to invoice impact.

2026-03-02 Jonas Rivera (Metering): Confirmed metering pipeline deduplication uses event-id + customer-timestamp header. Postback uploads from SignalGrid had device-generated IDs that collided across retries causing multiple unique IDs. Noted missing dedupe window for 'queued' uploads. Linked PR to add queue-id header handling.

2026-03-03 Billing (Ethan): Applied provisional credit of $12,300 to SignalGrid account pending root-cause. Informed customer that we will backfill corrected metering records and issue a final adjustment if needed. Asked customer to confirm acceptance of provisional credit.
2026-03-04 Customer (SignalGrid - Tara): Confirmed acceptance of provisional credit and requested a short writeup of the fix to share with their finance team.
2026-03-05 Ethan (Support): Marking ticket Resolved after final invoice adjustment processed and patch merged. Provide remediation summary and next steps.
investigation_notes: Metering pipeline analysis (metersrv) shows a spike of 1.45M token events between 2026-02-21 03:00Z and 2026-02-22 08:00Z attributable to org sg-9882. Many events lacked the 'queue-id' header that our dedupe worker expects.

Ingress logs: multiple retries from same device IP with distinct device_event_id values generated by SDK when buffer was flushed; SDK documented behaviour creates a new event_id on each retry causing dedupe miss.

Cross-region attribution: rapid postback fanout routed to eu-west when us-west pool was saturated, which multiplied visibility in billing aggregates due to cross-region multiply-counting in an older aggregator batch job (agg-v2).

Billing aggregation job (agg-v2) had a bug where it did not honor 'queued' flag and applied realtime pricing for all ingestion events when source was 'postback'. A hotfix was deployed to agg-v2 to respect the queued flag and apply batch pricing rules.
Related PRs: metersrv/pull/4123 adds queue-id header processing for dedupe; agg-v2/pull/877 adds queued flag handling; ingestion/pull/221 fixes retry event-id regeneration in SDK v1.8.
Risk assessment: Fix is low-risk, affects only postback processing path. Requires SDK patch release and a short migration notice to customers using offline buffering.
resolution: 2026-03-03: Provisional credit of $12,300 applied to SignalGrid account (visible in billing UI).
2026-03-04: metersrv hotfix merged (PR #4123) and deployed to prod: dedupe now checks for queue-id and aligns postback retries.
2026-03-04: agg-v2 hotfix deployed to respect 'queued' flag and apply batch pricing for queued postbacks.

2026-03-05: Final invoice adjustment processed: original invoice reissued with a $12,300 credit line; credit memo CM-2026-309 attached to customer account. Customer notified and confirmed receipt. Ticket closed.

Follow-up actions: Publish guidance for offline buffering SDK best-practices; create a migration notice for SDK v1.8 -> v1.8.1 to avoid event_id regeneration; add telemetry to billing alerts to detect similar postback spikes and auto-flag high-latency queues. Owner: Billing Eng (Ethan). Due: 2026-04-01.
